title: Winning with the Edge Token
subtitle: One small token decides who goes first, who wins ties and who wins a drawn game.
summary: The Edge token is the tie-breaker of Mythos. Learn its three powers, how passing first claims it, and how to time your pass so ties break your way.

steps.title: The Edge's three powers
steps.body: Whoever holds the [[Edge token]] **takes the first turn** of the Action phase, **wins every tied mission** in Mission evaluation, and **wins the game** if the final scores are level after Round 4. In a game decided by a point or two, those ties are often the whole game, so the Edge deserves as much thought as any card in your hand.
bullets: Leads: takes the first turn of the Round

visual.caption: You hold the Edge: first turn, tied missions, tied game.

steps.title: It starts at random
steps.body: At setup, a randomly chosen first player takes the Edge. That player's Missions sit 1st and 3rd in the Mission deck, they decide first on a [[mulligan]], and they take the first turn of Round 1. That is the only time luck decides it. From then on, the Edge changes hands one way only: by [[passing]].

visual.caption: Setup: a random first player starts with the Edge.

steps.title: First to pass takes it
steps.body: During the [[Action phase]], the first player to [[pass]] gains the Edge token, or keeps it if they already had it. Passing ends your Action phase for the Round, and the other player then takes **successive turns** until they pass too. The Edge you claim applies straight away, in this Round's Mission evaluation, and again for the first turn of the next Round.

callout.text: First to pass gains or keeps the Edge. After that, the other player keeps taking turns until they also pass.

steps.title: The trade-off
steps.body: Passing early locks in the tie-breaks, but it hands your opponent a free run: they can play card after card while you watch, adding Power exactly where it beats you by one. The Edge only matters on a tie. Passing late keeps your options open, but if your opponent passes first, every tie this Round and the first turn of the next one go to them.

callout.text: The Edge never beats more Power. If they finish one ahead, your tie-break is worth nothing.

visual.label: You passed first; they added just enough

steps.title: Reading the board
steps.body: Pass first when the board already favours you: if every mission you care about is level or ahead and your opponent has little Chakra left, the Edge turns those draws into wins. Keep playing when you're behind on a mission that matters, or when they still have the Chakra and cards to answer. Count their Chakra: with 3 left, they can't reveal a 4-cost Kakashi.
bullets: Level or ahead everywhere? Pass and take the ties
Behind where it matters? Keep playing
Count their Chakra before you pass

visual.label: Level board + the Edge = a win

steps.title: The final tie-break
steps.body: After Round 4, compare [[Mission points]]. The higher total wins, and if the totals are level the Edge holder wins the game. That makes the last pass a double prize: the first player to pass in Round 4 wins every tied mission, including the new A-rank mission worth base + 4, **and** a tied game.

callout.text: Going into Round 4, track the score. If you're level or one point behind, the Edge might be worth more than any card you could play.

widget.title: Edge Duel
widget.brief: Win a series of duels decided by the [[Edge token]] and the timing of your [[pass]]. Read each board, choose whether to keep playing or pass, and make sure the ties break your way.

quiz.prompt: Your opponent starts the Round holding the Edge. This Round you pass first. Who holds the Edge during Mission evaluation?
choices: You, because the first player to pass gains the Edge
Your opponent; the holder keeps it for the whole game
Nobody until the next Start phase
quiz.explanation: The first player to [[pass]] gains (or keeps) the [[Edge token]], and it applies to this Round's ties straight away.

quiz.prompt: You pass first. Your opponent still has 6 Chakra and several cards. What can they do?
choices: Play one more card, then the Round ends
Nothing; the Action phase ends when anyone passes
Take successive turns, one card at a time, until they pass
quiz.explanation: Once you've passed, your opponent keeps taking turns one after another until they [[pass]] too. That free run is the price of taking the Edge early.

quiz.prompt: After Round 4 the score is 15 to 15. Who wins?
choices: The player who won the A-rank mission
The player holding the Edge token
The player with more characters in play
quiz.explanation: A tied game goes to whoever holds the [[Edge token]] at the end, which is the player who passed first in Round 4.
